versioning: Additions and removals create theorems_v2.json; this file is never edited once a curve has been published against it. A published curve names the set file and its sha256, so a later set cannot silently redefine an earlier solved-rate. Correcting an authoring error is also a new version, with the correction recorded in the new file's `supersedes` note -- the same rule the corpus seeds follow.
held_out_definition: Absent from prover/sample_triples.json, the 155-row extraction the v0.6 tactic checkpoint was trained on: no theorem id below appears there, and no proposition below appears as any extracted stateBefore. tests/test_proof_curve.py asserts both, so 'held out' is checked rather than asserted.
solvability: Every theorem carries a `witness`: a tactic sequence, built only from the eight registered schemas, that closes it under live Lean. The witness is an AUTHORING ARTIFACT and is never shown to a search arm. Its purpose is to make the curve interpretable: an unsolved run is a ranking/search failure at that budget, never an impossible target.

init.note: Lean's prelude only; no Lake project is loaded.

proofcurve.note: Requires `lake build` in prover/lean/proofcurve first. PyPantograph 0.3.15's own LEAN_PATH discovery shells out to POSIX `printenv` and fails on Windows; passing lean_path explicitly bypasses that call entirely (prover/FEASIBILITY.md landmine 12). An Init-only server cannot even STATE these propositions -- `Unknown identifier ProofCurve.Both` -- which is what makes them a project-import family rather than decoration.

families.conjunction: Introduce, split a conjunctive goal, and reach premises through structure projections. Solutions lean on `constructor` + `projection`.
families.implication_chain: Curried arrow premises: bind several hypotheses accessibly, then close by `assumption`. Solutions use no projection at all -- the shape that makes this a different family rather than a longer version of the first.
families.disjunction: Choose a disjunct before discharging it. Solutions need `left`/`right`, which no other family requires.
families.project_import: Same underlying logic, stated through project-owned abbreviations. Lean's pretty printer does NOT unfold `ProofCurve.Both P Q`, so the conclusion is syntactically OPAQUE: a syntax-aware blind order sees an atom where a conjunction stands. This family is the deliberate stress on the v0.6 winner.
